question: At what temperature does water transform into steam under normal atmospheric pressure?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**100ºC (212ºF)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Water transforms into **steam** at a temperature of **100ºC (212ºF)** under **normal atmospheric pressure**, which is approximately **1 atm (101.325 kPa).**
 
• This process is called **boiling**, and it occurs when the **vapor pressure** of water equals the atmospheric pressure.
 
• At the boiling point, water molecules gain enough **kinetic energy** to overcome intermolecular forces and transition from the **liquid phase to the gaseous phase.**
 
• The boiling point of water can vary depending on **altitude and pressure**. At higher altitudes where pressure is lower, water boils at a temperature below **100ºC**.
 
• This temperature is widely used in **science, cooking, and industrial applications** to measure and control heat processes.
 
• The boiling point of water is a crucial reference point in the **Celsius temperature scale**, where it is defined as **100ºC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **50ºC (122ºF)**__

 __
 
• This temperature is far below the **boiling point** of water under normal atmospheric pressure.
 
• At **50ºC**, water remains in the **liquid state** and is often considered warm but not hot enough for steam formation.
 
• This temperature is commonly used in applications like **heating water for bathing** or **other domestic uses.**
 
 
 
• **80ºC (176ºF)**__
 __
 
• **80ºC** is still below the boiling point of water.
 
• Water at this temperature is considered hot and is often used in **cooking or beverage preparation**, like making tea or coffee.
 
• At this temperature, water may begin to exhibit signs of **evaporation**, but it does not boil or turn into steam under normal atmospheric pressure.
 
 
 
• **0ºC (32ºF)**__
 
 
• This is the **freezing point** of water under normal atmospheric pressure, not the boiling point.
 
• At **0ºC**, water transitions from a **liquid to a solid**, forming ice.
 
• This temperature is a key reference in the **Celsius and Fahrenheit scales**.
